title: Safeguarding Singapore's National and Elite Athletes from Misuse of Drugs
what_it_is: Safeguarding Singapore's National and Elite Athletes from Misuse of Drugs

sections.label: Anti-Doping Singapore established 2010
sections.summary: The Government established Anti-Doping Singapore as the national anti-doping authority in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The Government established Anti-Doping Singapore (ADS) as the national anti-doping authority in 2010.

sections.label: National athletes mandatory ADEL modules
sections.summary: All national athletes must complete modules on WADA's Anti-Doping Education and Learning Platform, and a database of over 9,000 Singapore-registered medications is updated monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Third, it is mandatory for all national athletes to complete modules on the World Anti-Doping Agency's e-learning platform called the Anti-Doping Education and Learning (ADEL) Platform, to deepen their understanding of clean sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The database contains more than 9,000 medications registered in Singapore and is updated monthly.

sections.label: Sanctions for anti-doping rule violations
sections.summary: ADS imposes sanctions on athletes who violate anti-doping rules, ranging from a few months to a lifetime ban depending on fault, intention, substance and aggravating circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Under the ADS, sanctions are imposed on athletes found to have violated anti-doping rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: These range from a few months to a lifetime ban, depending on the degree of fault, intention, type of substance used and aggravating circumstances.

sections.label: Coaches, values and sporting excellence
sections.summary: A speaker describes European sporting academies wanting to produce good individuals with good values, and says coaching and cooperation with schools and MOE have scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In my recent visit to Europe, where I visited a few sporting centres of excellence – if I may call them that – in terms of football, I think the consistent message that has been sent is that they – these academies, these football clubs – they want to produce and create excellent footballers but, more than that, they also want to produce good individuals, individuals with good values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: As much as the pursuit of sporting excellence is about fitness, technical competencies of each sport, it is very much also about values inculcation, the promulgation of values from one generation to the next.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In that vein, coaching, as well as the role that coaches play, is a very important role that cannot be overstated in the sporting fraternity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, there can be a lot of scope for us – ADS, SportSG, SNOC and the different sporting bodies – to work together with the schools and MOE without even going into specifics and, definitely, I thank the Member for his suggestion.
